sentences.text:
Author: B. Vijaysen Reddy
Bench: B. Vijaysen Reddy
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice B. Vijaysen Reddy
 Writ Petition No.1788 of 2023
Order

(ORAL):
This writ petition is filed to declare the action of respondents/police in detaining and torturing the petitioner day by day threatening him to clear the private finances/loans to respondents Nos. 9 to 12 as illegal and arbitrary.
2.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that petitioner is not an accused in any crime and the official respondents particularly respondent No.3 - Commissioner of Police, Warangal, is threatening the petitioner to repay alleged debt amounts to respondents Nos. 9 to 12 or otherwise leave Warangal town or else petitioner would have to face dire consequences.
3. Based on the written instructions, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home submitted that no criminal cases are registered against the petitioner and Station House Officer, Matwada Police Station has not threatened the petitioner to clear private finances/loan to respondent Nos. 9 to 12 nor interfered in day to day affairs of the petitioner.
It is stated that petitioner has approached this Court by suppressing the material facts.

F.I.R.No.546 of 2022 was registered on 13.12.2022 under Sections 406, 417, 420 r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC') of Hanamkonda Police Station, on complaint lodged by respondent No.9.
Syed Azeemuddin, husband of respondent No.12 lodged another complaint in F.I.R.No.627 of 2022 of A.J.Mills Colony, was registered under Sections 406, 417, 420 r/w 34 of IPC.
In both the above F.I.Rs, petitioner and others are accused.

In the above referred complaints lodged against the petitioner, it was stated that huge sums of money running into several lakhs of rupees have been collected from various individuals including respondents Nos. 9 to 12 promising handsome interest.

The petitioner and others promised to return debt amounts and later the complainants came to know that house of the petitioner was mortgaged to Bank of Baroda, and towards loan recovery, bank has initiated proceedings for auction of house of the petitioner about two years back as he failed to repay the loan.

It is also stated in counter affidavit of respondents Nos. 9 to 12 that State Bank of India, Balasamudram Branch, has lodged a complaint against the petitioner on 07.05.2019 in F.I.R.No.201 of 2019 of Subedari Police Station, under Section 420 of IPC.
4. Learned counsel for respondents Nos. 9 to 12 submitted that this writ petition is filed by indulging in suppressing all facts.

The petitioner knew that all these three F.I.Rs were registered against him,
Mohammed Riyazuddin vs The State Of Telangana And 11 Others on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67637571/
1 and inspite of cooperating with the police in investigation, petitioner has come to this Court with unclean hands.
5.

sentences.text: Taking into consideration the fact that F.I.R.No.546 of 2022 of Hanamkonda Police Station, was registered on 13.12.2022 and the same is pending investigation, this Court is not inclined to grant any relief to the petitioner.

6. Accordingly, Writ Petition is disposed of directing the police to comply with procedure contemplated under Section 41A of Cr.P.C., and follow the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar1, as the offences mentioned in the above referred F.I.Rs are punishable with imprisonment of less than 7 years.
